title: Mixed-precision calibration harness and drift-aware thresholding for quant profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable calibration harness that evaluates the quality impact of mixed-precision quantization profiles (AWQ and GPTQ at int8/int4) across representative workloads and automatically suggests workload-specific acceptance thresholds. The harness will: run controlled holdout evaluations, compute per-profile and per-workload deltas for a set of core metrics, surface calibration recommendations, and wire regression alerts into Redwood Console. The goal is to make quantization rollout decisions data-driven and reduce manual tuning effort while ensuring regressions are caught before customer impact.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness executes end-to-end for at least 3 model families (small, med, large) and produces a human-readable report
Per-workload thresholds generated for each quant profile (int8 AWQ, int4 AWQ, int8 GPTQ, int4 GPTQ) with confidence intervals
Console dashboard shows baseline vs quantized trajectories and fires an example regression alert during simulated drift
CI gating hook exists: PRs that change default quant profiles fail the gate if simulated regression > configured threshold
Runbook describing rollback triggers and safe fallback policies is published and linked in the report
implementation_notes: Create standardized holdout corpus covering: instruction-following, summarization, code generation, math reasoning, long-context chat, and retrieval-augmented Q&A
Instrument runner to capture: token-level log-prob distributions, final output texts, embeddings, and attention cache snapshots where feasible
Metrics: token perplexity delta, EM where applicable, ROUGE-L, BLEU (for code), embedding cosine similarity (SBERT), and KL divergence of token distributions
Per-layer sensitivity probe: ablate quantization in specific layers to compute influence scores and surface most sensitive components
Calibration algorithm: bootstrap sampling to compute 95% CIs, and Bayesian hierarchical model to recommend per-workload thresholds based on historical noise
Threshold policy: prefer conservative thresholds for high-traffic endpoints; allow more aggressive profiles for background batch jobs
Integration: push results to Console via metrics API and create an alert policy template (severity, runbook link, auto-tag)
test_plan: Baseline run: float32 model on holdout sets to establish reference metrics
Quant runs: int8 AWQ, int4 AWQ, int8 GPTQ, int4 GPTQ for each model family
Stress: Simulate prompt distribution shift by resampling 30% novel prompts and re-evaluate to validate drift detection
A/B gating simulation: apply thresholds to historical traffic trace and compute expected false positive/negative rates
Regression smoke: create synthetic regression case (deliberate quantization bug) to confirm Console alert generation and incident workflow
steps: 1) Curate holdout datasets and annotate evaluation slices
2) Implement evaluation runner and metric collectors in evals pipeline
3) Add per-profile config schema and metadata (profile id, quant backend, bitwidth)
4) Build calibration algorithm and threshold suggestion module
5) Integrate with Console: dashboard and alert template
6) Wire CI gating (GitHub Actions) to run quick-scan calibration on PRs that change profiles
7) Publish runbook and ship pilot to one internal team for feedback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Holdout sets may not capture customer distributions -> Mitigation: include diverse slices and solicit traffic logs from one pilot customer (anonymized)
Risk: Quant backend nondeterminism yields noisy metrics -> Mitigation: run each config N=5 times and use bootstrap CIs
Risk: False positives in alerts -> Mitigation: tune alert thresholds with historical traces and require sustained regression window (e.g., 30 mins)
decisions: Decision: Use both AWQ and GPTQ backends for calibration; do not prefer one by default until evidence accumulates
Decision: Produce per-workload thresholds rather than a single global threshold to reduce unnecessary rollbacks
Decision: Expose suggested threshold and conservative/experimental labels in Console so SRE/owners can choose rollout policy
notes: We will leverage existing quant evaluation infra where possible but build new slices for long-context chat and retrieval scenarios
Primary stakeholders: Quality (evals), Serving Runtime, Console, and a small set of product teams for pilot
Prototype demo targeted for 2026-03-20 internal demo; aim to close loop with pilot feedback by 2026-03-26
